releases.name: AkôFlow 1.0.12
releases.body:
## AkôFlow 1.0.12

This release integrates the daemon and Desktop improvements on matching frozen `v1.0.12` source tags.

### Changes

- Managed MCP connections for Codex, Claude Desktop, Claude Code and other AI apps, with separate permissions, enable/pause, credential rotation and revocation. See the [MCP setup guide](https://akoflow.com/docs/reference/mcp).
- Docker Hub image discovery and digest-pinned SIF imports through the daemon.
- Native algorithm inspection, editable versioned Go scheduling plugins and the documented MOHEFT Pareto plugin.
- Safer execution cancellation and explicit recovery, exact producer allocation restoration, bounded SSH lookup retries and direct cloud console commands.
- Dependency security updates, consistent API documentation and tested prototype protection for the documentation dependency without an upstream fix.
- Correct shutdown of Kubernetes activity metrics sampling, preserving final metrics, artifact manifests and activity exit status.

### Install or update

Download the package for your system below:

- **macOS:** universal `.dmg` for installation, with the `.zip` used by the updater.
- **Windows x64:** `setup.exe` installer or the separate `portable.exe`.
- **Linux x64:** `.AppImage` or `.deb`.

Docker Desktop is required on macOS and Windows. Linux requires Docker Engine with the Compose v2 plugin. Desktop downloads and verifies the matching runtime archives from this release and loads them into local Docker. Daemon and BuildKit archives are supplied for both Linux amd64 and arm64.

### Validation

- All integrated pull requests and the final daemon/Desktop checks passed; the documentation was deployed successfully.
- The complete release workflow passed for Windows x64, macOS universal, Linux x64 and both runtime architectures.
- Updater SHA512 manifests were checked against the generated packages. The downloaded amd64 runtime archives passed their SHA256 checks.
- The actual released amd64 daemon was started in an isolated Docker instance. Native scheduling algorithms were discovered, MOHEFT compiled inside the image, and live Docker Hub search returned results.
- The official MCP SDK probe and an independent external protocol client discovered **150 administration tools** and read daemon identity. Revoked credentials were rejected.

[Release build and provenance](https://github.com/UFFeScience/akoflow/actions/runs/41529065790) · [Downloads and installation guide](https://akoflow.com/docs/downloads)

releases.name: AkôFlow 1.0.11
releases.body:
## AkôFlow 1.0.11

### Performance and execution inspection
- Paginate execution history before joining activity and infrastructure aggregates.
- Load workflow and environment summaries for catalogs and selectors; fetch complete DAGs only when needed.
- Load execution logs, events, workspaces, and file catalogs on demand.
- Fetch one activity at a time and paginate lifecycle events and infrastructure history.
- Avoid overlapping monitor requests and duplicate cloud event reads.

### Documentation
- Add illustrated guides for the first local workflow execution and the Montage 050 scientific experiment, with downloadable examples and provenance.
- Document the new API read models and filters.

### Maintenance
- Update build dependencies and verify the existing dependency security mitigations.

## Installation
Docker Desktop is required on macOS and Windows; Linux requires Docker Engine and Compose v2.
- macOS: open the universal `.dmg` and move AkôFlow Desktop to Applications.
- Windows: use the x64 setup installer or portable executable.
- Linux: use the x64 `.AppImage` or `.deb`.

The daemon and BuildKit archives are loaded locally by Desktop. Updater manifests and runtime checksums are verified by the release workflow. Both application sources are frozen at tag `v1.0.11`.

releases.name: AkôFlow 1.0.10
releases.body:
## AkôFlow 1.0.10

This release integrates the execution, planning, transfer and Desktop improvements validated for the 1.0.10 release.

- Shared planning/SimGrid materialization stages, whole-workspace byte accounting and explicit calibration provenance.
- Per-dependency routing: mandatory cloud ↔ HPC relay; authenticated eligible cloud peers; proven shared HPC storage; exact-instance local copies.
- Verified compressed snapshots, reader-safe archive reuse, streaming extraction and conflict-safe consumer barriers.
- Safer recovery, exact cloud-generation SSH trust, bounded Slurm reconciliation and explicit CPU-capacity admission.
- Workflow-filtered execution pagination, Desktop navigation and runtime-version pinning.
- Runnable local workflow examples and verified physical output manifests.
- Dependency security updates and reproducible depth-limit mitigation for the unpatched upstream braces advisory.

### Validation and limitations

Go tests, native SimGrid tests, Desktop build/regressions and documentation checks were validated. Scientific profiles retain measured-versus-estimated provenance; this release does not claim global ±20% prediction accuracy. Recovered references are not independent cold-run benchmarks.

Upstream GHSA-vfj7-8cjw-p6xm has no patched braces version. A version-bound, fail-closed local patch is applied on installation, and CI verifies malicious patterns, direct AST depth and normal glob compatibility. The original version/advisory remains documented; the audit gate rejects other advisories.

### Functioning workflow screenshots

These are preserved reference screenshots of completed local Docker workflows, not newly executed cloud benchmarks.

**Completed ML workflow: five activities completed, with dependency staging visible.**

![Completed ML workflow](https://github.com/UFFeScience/akoflow/releases/download/v1.0.10/showcase-ml-workflow.png)

**RAG generated files: observed outputs with sizes and SHA-256 checksums.**

![Verified RAG generated files](https://github.com/UFFeScience/akoflow/releases/download/v1.0.10/showcase-rag-generated-files.png)

Screenshot integrity is provided in the attached screenshots.sha256 file.


### Reproducible packaging

Application source tags were not moved. The reviewed [packaging recipe](https://github.com/UFFeScience/akoflow/blob/68cbe07abab79706566a3e20705c68e898f90653/.github/workflows/gh-akf-new-release.yaml) rebuilds the frozen tags with distinct Windows setup/portable names and validates updater SHA-512 values against the distributed packages before upload. Core application code remains the tagged source; the packaging correction is explicit rather than hidden by rewriting a tag.


### Installation

Docker Desktop is required on macOS and Windows; Linux requires Docker Engine and Compose v2. Use the universal macOS DMG, the Windows portable executable or the separate setup installer, and the Linux AppImage or Debian package. Runtime archives are loaded locally by Desktop. Packages follow the project's unsigned-build configuration.

releases.name: v1.0.9
releases.body:
## Install AkôFlow Desktop

AkôFlow Desktop requires Docker Desktop on macOS and Windows, or Docker Engine with the Compose v2 plugin on Linux. Download the matching asset below:

- **macOS:** open the universal `.dmg`, drag AkôFlow Desktop to Applications, and launch it.
- **Windows:** run the x64 portable `.exe` asset without an installation wizard.
- **Linux:** run the x64 `.AppImage` after `chmod +x`, or install the `.deb` with `sudo apt install ./Akoflow-Desktop-*.deb`.

The matching source is the Git tag `v1.0.9`. The runtime Docker archives in this release are loaded locally by Desktop; AkôFlow does not publish daemon or BuildKit packages to a container registry.
